content.title: About
content.content: Liquid stevia is a natural sweetener derived from the leaves of the Stevia rebaudiana plant. It is 200–300 times sweeter than sugar but contains virtually no calories and does not raise blood glucose levels. It is used in beverages, baked goods, sauces, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stevia has been used by indigenous peoples of South America for over a thousand years.
The first commercial stevia product appeared in Japan in the 1970s.
The liquid form allows precise dosing and even distribution in recipes.
Stevia does not cause tooth decay, unlike sugar.
Unlike artificial sweeteners, stevia is considered safe by EFSA and FDA.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: Liquid stevia provides virtually no calories, helping with weight management.

items.title: Does not raise blood sugar
items.content: Stevia’s glycemic index is close to zero, making it suitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Stevia leaves are rich in antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports blood pressure
items.content: Studies suggest stevia may help lower blood pressure.

items.title: Non‑cariogenic
items.content: Unlike sugar, stevia does not feed oral bacteria that cause cavities.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to stevia.

items.title: Bitter aftertaste
items.content: Exceeding recommended amounts can produce a characteristic bitter aftertaste.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Stevia may enhance the effect of certain antihypertensive drugs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Add a few drops of liquid stevia to tea, coffee, smoothies, sauces, or dough. For baking, typically use 1 ml of stevia instead of 1 tbsp of sugar, adjusting to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 12 months. Discard if the smell or taste changes.
